newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Handlowy IPO seen priced in mid-range.
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Handlowy IPO seen priced in mid-range.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy public offering price range is at a moderate discount to large listed banks and its final strike price is seen in the middle of the 28-35 zloty band, analysts said on Monday.

"It is an average range, one has to offer a discount for a company that is entering the bourse...I think the price will be somewhere around 30-31 zlotys, in the middle (of the range)," said Andrzej Soldek of ING BSK Asset Management.

Analysts said at 35 zlotys Handlowy's valuation would be similar to the Warsaw bourse's largest banks with its price-to-book value ratio at 1.6 and price-to-earnings ratio of 5.8 of 1997 expected earnings.
They said 28 zlotys would be a very attractive valuation with the bank's P/BV at 1.3 and P/E of 4.6.

Krzysztof Opawski, the head of Schroder Polska sp zoo, the Polish unit of the Handlowy offer global manager, told a news conference earlier on Monday, Handlowy should trade on bourse at a slight discount to banks with strategic foreign investors and at a premium to banks which lacked strategic partners.
"We believe that the market should value Bank Handlowy between the two groups, above the banks with no foreign investors and below those which have strategic partners," Opawski said.

Opawski said that in its evaluation Schroders took into account other banks' and Handlowy's earnings forecasts for 1997 and 1998 and their book values at end of 1996 and 1997 and assumed that Handlowy should open 20 percent above the issue price.
He said that according to book value Handlowy was being offered cheaper than other Polish, Hungarian and western European banks and was more expensive than Czech banks.
Earnings forecasts made it similarily priced to Czech banks and the six largest Polish listed banks but cheaper than Hungarian and western European banking stocks.
Opawski said the valuations already priced in Handlowy's convertible bond issue, which would eventually increase the number of its shares to 93 million from present 65 million.
Handlowy's President Cezary Stypulkowski, also present, said the bank was satisfied with the price range.
"The range might have been tighter but given our market's development the spread is acceptable," he told reporters.
The final strike price will be announced on June 17 following book-building for institutional investors.

Analysts expected the offer to succeed but saw Handlowy having bigger appeal to international investors keen to get a piece of Poland's economic success story than to retail players who might find the 300 million zloty retail tranche too big.

Some said however, that a set of incentives for small players and concerted marketing campaign might help mobilise petty savers on a scale unseen since Warsaw bourse's buying frenzy in late 1993 and early 1994.

Analysts said the ability to reach the top of the price range would be hampered by general bearish outlook for Polish banks' profits in 1997 and a looming competition from another giant offering of KGHM Polska Miedz copper concern due in July.
Some analysts said the offer would be helped if Handlowy managed to announce a group of long-term institutional players before the end of the May 26-June 13 subscription period.

Stypulkowski said Handlowy has already picked three international financial institutions to which it would offer jointly up to 42.9 percent of shares but the final decision rested with the treasury ministry.
